canonical_name: Behrend lower-bound construction for three-term-progression-free integer sets
canonical_statement: For every positive real epsilon, for all sufficiently large natural N, the maximum cardinality of a subset of the nonnegative integers at most N containing no three distinct terms in arithmetic progression is strictly greater than N raised to 1 - (2 * sqrt(2 * log 2) + epsilon) / sqrt(log N).

source_selection.citation: F. A. Behrend, On Sets of Integers Which Contain No Three Terms in Arithmetical Progression, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 32(12) (1946), 331-332, DOI 10.1073/pnas.32.12.331, PMCID PMC1078964

boundary_cases.empty_and_singleton_sets: Remain valid object-model cases. Whether they satisfy the quantitative inequality depends on N and epsilon, and the eventual quantification does not require small N.
boundary_cases.constant_or_repeated_triples: Allowed and treated as trivial; the source predicate excludes only pairwise-distinct triples, and the checked Nat transport proves exact agreement with ThreeAPFree.
boundary_cases.inclusive_endpoint: N itself is included through rothNumberNat (N + 1); replacing it by rothNumberNat N is the boundary mutation.
boundary_cases.rounding: The natural extremal cardinality is cast to Real before the strict comparison; no rounding operation is inserted.
